removal_suggestion: Do not present the constraints as an immediately separable choice for each enzyme; describe the catalog as an adversarial 3-partite exact-cover instance and explicitly state that catalog order and resource incidence may force extensive backtracking. common_affordance: The requirement to select exactly one triple for each enzyme while simultaneously covering each substrate and profile exactly once, which permits a fixed-enzyme recursive search with substrate/profile bitmasks.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its DLX exact-cover search still has exponential worst-case behavior on dense or adversarial 3-dimensional instances and timed out.
It explicitly tries permutations of the catalog, giving factorial or worse growth instead of exploiting the three-way matching structure, and timed out.
Its proposed mask-based DP implementation terminated with a runtime error before producing an answer.

recommended_edit: Add a mutable adversarial-instance requirement: state that the catalog may be ordered adversarially and that official tests include dense instances with many partial selections that fail only near the final enzyme, while leaving the input, output, bounds, and required protocol unchanged. This most directly attacks the surviving fixed-order backtracking search.
